brief_intent.critique: The screen substantively delivers the core brief: a stats sidebar with level, XP bar, and available skill points; a clear title; and a connected-node skill tree as the visual centerpiece. However, the intended experience is weakened in two ways. First, the 'states' legend (Learned, Mastered, Locked, Path, Active) is not visibly instantiated on the nodes—nearly every node looks like the same 'Learned' gold/blue fill, so the user cannot distinguish mastered vs. locked vs. active skills, breaking the relationship between the legend and the tree. visual_system_craft.critique: The skill-tree centerpiece has severe construction and alignment failures that break the system. (1) The connecting 'path' lines are inconsistent: the Pyromancy column uses a thick orange stroke, Arcanum a thin blue stroke, Glaciurgy a thin cyan stroke, and Shadowweave a thick gold stroke—stroke weight and color do not follow a single grammar, and the gold lines cross/overlap the cyan and blue nodes in the center, creating visual collisions and unclear z-order. (2) Node vertical alignment is ragged: the four columns do not share a consistent row grid (e.g., the top row nodes sit at slightly different y-positions, and the central 'Mastered' nodes float off-grid), so the matrix reads as hand-placed rather than a disciplined tree. (3) The 'LV 1' / 'LV 3' labels are inconsistently placed—some sit directly under the node, some overlap the connecting line, and the central node's label collides with the gold path. (4) Node state styling is muddled: 'Learned' (gold), 'Mastered' (teal), and 'Locked' (dim) are not visually distinct enough from the branch-colored nodes, and the dashed 'Active' ring only appears on a few nodes without a clear rule. (5) The legend at the bottom uses small dots that do not match the actual node rendering (size, glow, ring), so the legend does not accurately represent the system. (6) Typography: the 'LV 1' labels are tiny, low-contrast, and inconsistent in weight against the larger serif node icons; the sidebar mixes a serif display (Sylvara, 3 available) with a monospace label face and a sans body without a clear scale, and the XP bar's '18,420 / 24,000' uses a monospace that feels disconnected from the rest. (7) Spacing rhythm in the sidebar is uneven: the gap between the stat cards (Power/Vitality/Focus/Resolve) and the Loadout section is larger than the gap between the stat cards themselves, and the empty-slot rows have inconsistent vertical padding. (8) The corner bracket decorations appear on the sidebar and main panel but not consistently (top-left of sidebar vs. top-right of header), fragmenting the frame language.
visual_system_craft.suggestion: Prioritize a single, rigorous node-and-path grammar. (1) Define one path style: uniform stroke weight (e.g., 2px), a neutral 'path' color (muted gold or desaturated teal) for all connections, with branch color reserved for the node fill only; route lines on a clean grid with no node overlaps and a consistent z-order (lines behind nodes). (2) Snap all nodes to a shared row/column grid so the four branches align horizontally; center the central 'Mastered' nodes on the grid and give them a distinct, larger treatment. (3) Standardize node labels: fixed position (centered below node, 8px gap), consistent size/weight, and a subtle background or letter-spacing so they never collide with paths. (4) Establish a clear 3-state node system—Locked (desaturated, no glow, thin ring), Learned (full branch color, soft glow, solid ring), Mastered (branch color + inner check + brighter glow + thicker ring)—and make the 'Active/selected' state a single, obvious affordance (e.g., animated dashed ring) applied uniformly. (5) Rebuild the legend to use actual node swatches (same size, glow, and ring as in the tree) so it accurately documents the system. (6) Lock a type scale: one display serif for the title and key numbers, one sans for body/labels, and reserve monospace only for numeric readouts (XP, counts) at a consistent size; increase 'LV' label contrast and unify weight. (7) Normalize sidebar spacing to a 4/8px rhythm: equal gaps between stat cards, a defined section gap before Loadout, and consistent row padding for equipped and empty slots. (8) Apply the corner-bracket frame treatment consistently to all major panels (sidebar, header, main canvas, legend) or remove it entirely for a cleaner system.
